problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $P(0,-2,-4)$ and $Q(5,0,1).$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Equation of the Line Passing Through Two Given Points
examples.problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $P(1,-1,2)$ and $Q(3,2,7).$
examples.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $P$ and parallel to $\mathbf{v}$ is given by

$$
\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{p} + t \mathbf{v},
$$

where $t \in (-\infty, \infty)$ and $\mathbf{p}$ is the position vector of $P.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $P(1,-1,2)$ and $Q(3,2,7),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =⟨3,2,7⟩-⟨1,-1,2⟩ \\  & =⟨2,3,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Find a vector equation of the straight line passing through $P(1,-\sqrt{2},-3)$ and parallel to $v=[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 9 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $P$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=p+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $p$ is the position vector of $P.$

In our case, the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -\sqrt{2} \\ -3\end{aligned}].$

Using the formula for the vector equation of a line, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -\sqrt{2} \\ -3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 9 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
